newsitem.title: UK: British Gas loses custom as deregulation widens.
newsitem.headline: British Gas loses custom as deregulation widens.

text.p: The first day of domestic deregulation of the British gas market in the west of England test area of Dorset and the former county of Avon has seen 6,417 customers switching from British Gas Plc to new suppliers, the company's pipeline arm TransCo said in a statement.

This figure will rise to 13,199 by Wednesday. 500,000 consumers can choose new gas suppliers from Monday, and a further 1 million in Kent and East and West Sussex can do so from March 7, Transco said.

"Providing choice to the consumer is the biggest challenge facing the gas industry at present. Today is a major milestone and one which keeps us all on track to provide competition nationwide next year," said Roger Garner, TransCo director.

TransCo added that in the first pilot area of domestic deregulation, launched in April last year in Devon, Cornwall and Somerset, 92,600 consumers out of a total of around 500,000, have already switched suppliers.
